parsed.explanation: The combined regime makes trans visitors' exposure severe and partly unavoidable: federal passport and visa screening require birth-sex consistency and can trigger refusal, stranding or fraud bars; many facilities restrict or criminalize identity-incongruent restroom use, with a documented arrest and misgendered custody. National custody reports describe forced labor, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse for detained trans people, and official language frames pro-trans advocacy as terrorism. Limited litigation and some protections create partial relief but do not offset active federal and state rules. Adult and minor travellers face the same entry screening; a minor can also encounter school-facility and care restrictions.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal passports bar new X or nonmatching markers; valid X expire only. Visa/entry screening treats document discrepancies or reasonable doubt about sex as refusal grounds and may pursue material fraud, producing stranding or lifetime ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing valid X passports remain accepted until expiry; litigation, legal-aid FAQs and some injunctions contest the regime, but operative passport and screening policy remain documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Passport or record mismatch can trigger questioning, denial, detention and then hostile custody.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections mandate short hair, HRT removal and psychiatric treatment for trans inmates; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse, with reporting of trans prisoners stopped.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented individualized safe placement, medication continuity, consular monitoring or effective complaint system. General rule of law may restrain some measures, but not established here.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border refusal or facility arrest can funnel a visitor into the documented custody environment.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal rules limit government-funded single-sex facilities to birth sex; multiple jurisdictions restrict government, school, college and some private facilities; one statute criminalizes refusal to depart a mismatched public restroom, with documented arrest and men's-ward detention.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Some jurisdictions lack mapped bans, and municipal ordinances exist, but they are not nationwide and do not override federal facility rules or criminal enforcement.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal, state and municipal rules interact so restroom/shelter access is conditional and, in some places, arrestable.

care_services.exposure: Minors' gender-affirming care is banned in many jurisdictions including the division; funding, school and insurance measures chill care. Adult visitor emergency care, HRT continuity and ward placement are not documented.
care_services.protection: No documented traveller-facing care shield, rapid medication access or ward-placement guarantee. Ordinary clinical services may exist, but government-funded spaces and minors' services are restricted.
care_services.interaction: Illness, injury or medication checks can bring custody, border screening or facility enforcement into contact with care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism language labels radical gender ideology and pro-trans groups as terrorism, while public opinion supports birth-sex documents and restrictions; this legitimizes exclusion and can shape border, police and facility enforcement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime law, employment rulings, some court injunctions and statements that mere disagreement is not targeted may offer recourse, but are not traveller-service guarantees.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Functioning courts may help, yet when institutions enforce hostile rules the same rule-of-law machinery intensifies exposure.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors face the same federal document screening and, in the division, public-school bathroom restrictions and minors' care bans; guardians may encounter scrutiny, but actual visitor enforcement cases are not reported.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented guardian shield, school-facility override, rapid care access, or family complaint mechanism for travelling minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Parent and child are assessed together at entry; a school or health encounter can out the child and escalate to custody.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No current quantified trans street-violence pattern or organised sweeps are documented; risk is elevated by hostile rhetoric, a facility arrest example, and border/custody enforcement.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime coverage, municipal ordinances and employment rulings may give some recourse after violence, but no documented prevention of refusal, arrest or custody abuse.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Calling police for safety could require documents and expose identity to the same hostile rules.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Effective complaints for border refusal, facility exclusion, immigration custody abuse or care continuity are not documented; enforcement rates, hospital placement and nonbinary marker handling remain unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid guidance, ongoing suits, blocked injunctions and some local service protections show possible relief, but operational reliability for travellers is not documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation may modify the regime, but the present traveller must pass federal and state rules before any remedy is reached.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier-1 institutional exclusion, but worse in severity: federal border screening, immigration-custody abuse and counterterrorism threat framing are added. Some national protections and litigation keep it slightly above a purely local rule without custody violence.

Lower than 0.35-B. That case documents humiliating birth-sex placement with inadequate remedy; here the same exposure is combined with entry refusal/fraud bars, a documented criminal arrest, custody abuse and national hostile framing.

Below 0.45-A. That elevated case has a birth-sex facility rule but no organised arrests, custody abuse or immigration fraud bars; this combined regime includes documented arrest, misgendered detention and severe custody harm.

parsed.synthesis: Documented federal passport/visa sex-marker rules make outing at entry likely for visibly trans travellers and can trigger refusal, stranding or fraud bars. Once inside, many government facilities enforce birth-sex access, with a state arrest and misgendered custody showing real criminal exposure. Border or facility escalation can meet immigration-custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse. Official counterterrorism language and major public opinion further degrade safety. National hate-crime, employment rulings and ongoing litigation are climate signals and possible relief, but do not offset operative traveller-facing restrictions. For minors, school-facility and care bans add uncertainty without documented visitor enforcement.
